items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing the New York State Paperwork Reduction Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7865

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing the New
York State Paperwork Reduction Act


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To reduce the overall burden on businesses, individuals, and local
governments to comply with regulations and mandates to submit
information to state agencies and to improve the information
management practices of state government.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends the Executive Law to add a new article 43, which
would constitute the New York State Paperwork Reduction Act. This
section would:

* Authorize the Governor's Office of Regulatory Reform (GORR) to
oversee the use of information resources by the Executive Branch and
Authorities in order to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of
governmental operations, including burden reduction and service
delivery to the public;

* Set overall paperwork reduction goals for all state agencies of 10%
through FYs 2011-2012, and 5% each during FYs 2013 through 2016;

* Make reforms on the agency level to permit compliance with this act;

* Amend the rule-making process so that GORR must review an agency's
proposed information collection process and may disapprove of new
information collection in certain limited circumstances;

* Authorize GORR to designate a central collection agency to obtain
information for two or more agencies;

* Authorize GORR to direct agencies to share their information with
other agencies to prevent duplication of collection, provided such
directive does not violate another statute;

* Empower GORR to make periodic reviews and recommendations of
agencies' information resources management activities;

* Require GORR to make an annual report of its activities under this
article to the Governor and the Legislature; and

* Authorize GORR to promulgate rules to enforce this article.

Section 2 establishes an effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently, state agencies collect a large amount of information from
businesses, individuals, and local governments. Much of this
information is reduplicative and unnecessary. In general, the
information management practices of state government are often
inefficient, redundant, and in many cases antiquated. This bill would
modernize the state's information collection procedures while also
mandating a reduction in the burden placed on regulated persons and
businesses to prepare and submit forms and reports to state agencies.
This bill is modeled on the popular and successful federal Paperwork
Reduction Act, which resulted in substantial burden reductions on a

federal level. This bill would bring the same long overdue efficiency
to state government.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New legislation.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Assistance to state agencies in implementation of such an initiative
is within the mission of Office for Technology and should be able to
be achieved as a priority within available resources. It is
anticipated that substantial savings shall be achieved not only by
individual state agencies, but by private sector entities who shall
see reduced compliance costs.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT in relation to requiring a study and report on methods to modernize information collection, retention and dissemination practices in the state; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7865A

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
in relation to
requiring a study and report on methods to modernize information
collection, retention and dissemination practices in the state; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

PURPOSE:
This legislation provides for a study and report, a first
step in enacting plans to reduce the paperwork burden on entities
doing business with the State, which would examine the following
issues:

a) information resource management policies and guidelines and the
possibility of developing uniform policies and guidelines in this area;

b) how information is collected and retained by state agencies and
what potential there is to modernize these functions in order to
reduce paper waste and cost to the state agencies;

c) how information is made available to the public and whether
opportunities to modernize, reduce paper waste, and reduce cost exist;

d) the best ways to modernize the information resource systems to
reduce waste and cost while maintaining privacy, confidentiality, an
security of information as needed or required and what challenges
exist in this area;

e) whether information technology solutions exist to address the needs
of the state agencies regarding lowering waste and cost in their
information management systems.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Section 1. Establishes that he director of the office for technology,
in conjunction with the director of budget, the director of state
operations, and the secretary of state, and in consultation with the
state comptroller, shall study and issue a comprehensive report on
methods to modernize the information collection, retention, and
dissemination practices of agencies in the state.

In addition this section establishes the contents· of the report as
described above, the due date for the report and the report recipients

Section 2. provides for the enacting date and the date that the act
is appealed, April 1, 2012.

JUSTIFICATION:
Reducing costs associated with paperwork both internal
to agencies and for those filing forms and reports with agencies

continues to be a goal that will save the state and filers money,
enable the state to be more
transparent, and assist businesses in viewing the State as a partner
rather than an obstacle to creating jobs and meeting their compliance
obligations.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Within available resources of the agencies
resulting in cost savings plans.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
